'''{{Langr|fi|Hannu Rajaniemi}}''' (born 9 March 1978) is a Finnish-born writer and [[biotechnology]] entrepreneur. He has published literary works in [[fantasy]] and [[science fiction]], and writes in both English and [[Finnish language|Finnish]]. 

==Early life and education==
Rajaniemi was born in [[Ylivieska]], Finland, in 1978. 

He holds a BSc in mathematics from the [[University of Oulu]], a [[Certificate of Advanced Study in Mathematics]] from the [[University of Cambridge]] and a PhD in [[mathematical physics]] from the [[University of Edinburgh]]. Prior to starting his PhD candidature, he completed his [[national service]] as a research scientist for the [[Finnish Defence Forces]].<ref name=TTM/>

While pursuing his PhD in Edinburgh, Rajaniemi joined Writers' Bloc,<ref>{{Cite web | url=http://www.writers-bloc.org.uk/comrades/hannu-rajaniemi/ | title=Writers' Bloc » Hannu Rajaniemi | date=4 January 2010 | publisher=Writers' Bloc | access-date=7 January 2015 | archive-date=10 November 2014 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141110063440/http://www.writers-bloc.org.uk/comrades/hannu-rajaniemi/ | url-status=dead }}</ref> a writers' group in Edinburgh that organizes semi-regular [[spoken-word]] performances and {{citation needed span|date=May 2026|text=counts [[Charles Stross]] amongst its members.}}

==Literary career==
Early works include his first published short story, "Shibuya No Love",<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20050204085029/http://www.futurismic.com/fiction/shibuya.html "Shibuya no Love"].</ref> in 2003 and his short story "Deus Ex Homine" in [[Nova Scotia: New Scottish Speculative Fiction|Nova Scotia]], a 2005 [[anthology]] of Scottish science fiction and fantasy, which caught the attention of his current literary agent, John Jarrold.<ref name=SFN>{{Cite web |url=https://www.scifinow.co.uk/news/interview-hannu-rajaniemi/ |title=Interview: Hannu Rajaniemi |author = Bandah, Sam |publisher=SciFiNow |date=3 November 2010 |access-date=7 January 2015}}</ref><ref>[http://www.johnjarrold.co.uk/clients/ John Jarrold: Clients]. Retrieved 19 December 2017.</ref>

Rajaniemi gained attention in October 2008 when Jarrold secured a three-book deal for him with [[Victor Gollancz Ltd|Gollancz]],<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://jjarrold.livejournal.com/29142.html |title=Major three-book pre-empt deal for debut SF novelist |date=6 October 2008 |access-date=7 January 2015 |first=John |last=Jarrold |publisher=[[LiveJournal]] |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120316002650/http://jjarrold.livejournal.com/29142.html |archive-date=16 March 2012 }}</ref> on the basis of only twenty-four double-spaced pages.<ref name=SFN/><ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.theguardian.com/books/2010/nov/09/hannu-rajaniemi-quantum-thief | title= Hannu Rajaniemi: the science of fiction| author= Lea, Richard | work= [[The Guardian]] | access-date=7 January 2015 | location=London | date=9 November 2010}}</ref>
His debut novel, ''[[The Quantum Thief]]'', was published in September 2010 by Gollancz in Britain<ref>[http://www.orionbooks.co.uk/authors/rajaniemi-hannu Hannu Rajaniemi] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100406034946/http://www.orionbooks.co.uk/authors/rajaniemi-hannu |date=6 April 2010 }} on the publisher's site.</ref> and was published in May 2011 by [[Tor Books]] in the U.S.<ref>{{Cite web| url=http://www.johnjarrold.co.uk/news/310/three-book-us-rights-deal-for-hannu-rajaniemi/ | title=Three-book US rights deal for Hannu Rajaniemi | author= Jarrold, John |date=23 July 2010 |access-date=7 January 2015}}</ref><ref name=jussi>Jussi Ahlroth, Hannu Rajaniemen romaanit julkaistaan myös Yhdysvalloissa, Helsingin Sanomat, 20 July 2010, p. B 1.</ref> The novel was nominated for the 2011 [[Locus Award for Best First Novel]].<ref name=locus>{{Cite web|url=http://www.locusmag.com/News/2011/05/2011-locus-award-finalists/| title=2011 Locus Award Finalists| date=11 May 2011| publisher=[[Locus (magazine)|Locus]]| access-date=13 May 2011}}</ref> A sequel, ''[[The Fractal Prince]]'', was published in September 2012 by Gollancz in Britain, and in October 2012 by Tor in the U.S.<ref>[http://upcoming4.me/media-news/book-news/item/9332-hannu-rajaniemi-the-fractal-prince-cover-art,-release-date,-and-preorder-details Hannu Rajaniemi – The Fractal Prince cover art, release date, and preorder details] on Upcoming4.me. {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120414164651/http://www.upcoming4.me/media-news/book-news/item/9332-hannu-rajaniemi-the-fractal-prince-cover-art,-release-date,-and-preorder-details |date=14 April 2012 }}.</ref> The third book in the series,  ''[[The Causal Angel]]'', was published in July 2014 by Gollancz in the U.K. and by Tor in the U.S.<ref>[http://www.tor.com/blogs/2014/07/book-review-the-causal-angel-hannu-rajaniemi Endgame: The Causal Angel by Hannu Rajaniemi].</ref> A standalone espionage procedural, ''[[Summerland (2018 novel)|Summerland]]'' was published in 2018 to a mixed reception.<ref name=locus2>{{cite web |work=[[Locus Magazine]] |title=Amy Goldschlager Reviews ''Summerland'' Audiobook by Hannu Rajaniemi |url=https://locusmag.com/review/amy-goldschlager-reviews-summerland-audiobook-by-hannu-rajaniemi/ |date=March 11, 2019 |first=Amy |last=Goldschlager |accessdate=September 6, 2026}}</ref><ref name=kirkus>{{cite web|url=https://www.kirkusreviews.com/book-reviews/hannu-rajaniemi/summerland-rajaniemi/ |work=[[Kirkus Reviews]] |title=''SUMMERLAND'' |date=April 16, 2018|accessdate=September 6, 2026}}</ref>

Rajaniemi took inspiration from the literary works of [[Jules Verne]] in both his career in science and his science-fiction writing.<ref>[http://www.study.eu/article/popular-finnish-authors-reveal-the-books-that-shaped-their-student-years Popular Finnish authors reveal the books that shaped their student years]. [http://www.study.eu/ Study.eu]. Retrieved 19 December 2017.</ref> Other influences include [[Maurice Leblanc]], [[Arthur Conan Doyle]] and architecture blogger [[BLDGBLOG|Geoff Manaugh]].<ref>[http://www.iop.org/careers/working-life/profiles/page_57724.html "Once a Physicist: Hannu Rajaniemi"].</ref> 

==Business career==

Rajaniemi co-founded Helix [[nanotechnologies]].<ref>[https://www.snappr.co/ycdb/helix-nanotechnologies Helix Nanotechnologies]. The Y Combinator Database. Retrieved 19 December 2017.</ref>

He is the founding director of a commercial research organisation ThinkTank Maths.<ref name=TTM>{{Cite web |url=https://thinktankmaths.com/about/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080612180907/http://thinktankmaths.com/about/ | title=About us | publisher=ThinkTank Maths| access-date=7 January 2015 |archive-date=12 June 2008}}</ref> He cofounded the biotechnology company [[Helix Nano]] with Nikolai Eroshenko in 2013.<ref>{{cite news |last=Newitz|first=Annalee|date=4 August 2016|title=Hannu Rajaniemi leads a double life as a scientist and sci-fi writer|url=https://arstechnica.com/gaming/2016/08/submarines-spaceships-startups-and-sci-fi-the-life-of-hannu-rajaniemi/|work=[[Ars Technica]] |access-date=1 December 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Clifford|first=Catherine |date=24 April 2020 |title=What It's Like to Invent a Coronavirus Vaccine in the Middle of a Pandemic|url=https://www.cnbc.com/2020/04/24/what-it-is-like-to-invent-a-covid-19-vaccine-during-pandemic.html | publisher = [[CNBC]] |access-date=1 December 2025}}</ref> Rajaniemi is the co-founder of [[Red Queen Bio]], a startup aimed at countering the threat of AI bioweapons that spun out of Helix Nano and which attracted investment from [[OpenAI]] in a $15 million seed round in 2025.<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.reuters.com/technology/openai-backs-startup-aiming-block-ai-enabled-bioweapons-2025-11-13/ |title=OpenAI backs startup aiming to block AI-enabled bioweapons |date=November 13, 2025 |work=Reuters |first=Deepa |last=Seetharaman}}</ref>

==Awards and honors==
* 2012 [[Tähtivaeltaja Award]], winner (best science-fiction book published in Finnish language) for ''[[The Quantum Thief]]''.<ref>[https://partialrecall.blogspot.com/2012/06/tahtivaeltaja-award-to-hannu-rajaniemi.html "Tähtivaeltaja Award 2012"]</ref>
* 2011 [[Science Fiction & Fantasy Translation Awards]], winner, Short Form category, translation of Hannu Rajaniemi's [https://web.archive.org/web/20101205004929/http://subterraneanpress.com/index.php/magazine/spring-2010/fiction-elegy-for-a-young-elk-by-hannu-rajaniemi "Elegy for a Young Elk"].<ref>[http://www.sfftawards.org/?p=424 "And The Winners Are…"], SF&FTA website, 18 June 2011.</ref>
* 2011 [[Locus Award for Best First Novel]], nominee, ''[[The Quantum Thief]]''<ref name=locus/>
* 2011 [[John W. Campbell Memorial Award]], third place, ''[[The Quantum Thief]]''<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.locusmag.com/SFAwards/Db/Cmem2011.html |title=The Locus Index to SF Awards: 2011 John W. Campbell Memorial Award |work=[[Locus (magazine)|Locus]] |access-date=23 November 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121025143229/http://locusmag.com/SFAwards/Db/Cmem2011.html |archive-date=25 October 2012 |url-status=dead }}</ref>
* 2013 [[John W. Campbell Memorial Award]], nominee, ''[[The Fractal Prince]]''<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.locusmag.com/News/2013/05/campbell-memorial-award-finalists/ |title=Campbell Memorial Award Finalists |work=[[Locus (magazine)|Locus]] | date= 10 May 2013 | access-date=16 May 2013 }}</ref>

==Personal life==
{{As of|2014}}, Rajaniemi lived in [[San Francisco]], [[California]], with his wife.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.keskipohjanmaa.fi/uutiset/379872/Hannu-Rajaniemi-vastaanotti-Pro-Ylivieska-mitalin |title=Hannu Rajaniemi vastaanotti Pro Ylivieska-mitalin |date=16 December 2014 |website=[[Keskipohjanmaa]] |language=fi |access-date=17 March 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210317204608/https://www.keskipohjanmaa.fi/uutiset/379872/Hannu-Rajaniemi-vastaanotti-Pro-Ylivieska-mitalin |archive-date=17 March 2021}}</ref> Before moving to the U.S., he lived in the United Kingdom for over ten years.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://finlandabroad.fi/web/gbr/current-affairs/-/asset_publisher/4ojVRXvbDRVa/content/hannu-rajaniemi-pyrkii-valloittamaan-maailman/384951 |title=Hannu Rajaniemi aims at world domination |last=Heinilä |first=Tiina |date=12 October 2010 |publisher=[[Embassy of Finland, London]] |access-date=17 March 2021}}</ref>
